Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১) Most common cause of angina pectoris
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The most common cause of angina pectoris is atherosclerosis of the coronary arteries, which causes fixed narrowing of the vessel lumen. During increased myocardial oxygen demand (e.g., exercise), blood flow becomes inadequate, resulting in ischemic chest pain (stable angina).

Exam pearl:

  • Most common cause of angina → Coronary atherosclerosis

  • Most common cause of acute myocardial infarction → Coronary thrombosis on a ruptured atherosclerotic plaque

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২) Most important modifiable risk factor of coronary artery disease(CAD)
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Smoking is considered the most important modifiable risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD). It accelerates atherosclerosis, causes endothelial dysfunction, increases platelet aggregation, and promotes coronary thrombosis, markedly increasing the risk of myocardial infarction and sudden cardiac death.

Exam pearl:
Major modifiable CAD risk factors:

  • Smoking (most important)

  • Hypertension

  • Diabetes mellitus

  • Dyslipidaemia

  • Obesity

  • Physical inactivity

Smoking cessation is the single most effective lifestyle intervention to reduce CAD risk.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩) Vessels used in coronary artery bypass grafting except
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The vessels commonly used for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) are:

  • Internal mammary (internal thoracic) artery → most preferred due to excellent long-term patency

  • Radial artery → commonly used arterial graft

  • Great saphenous vein → most commonly used venous graft

The brachial artery is not used as a CABG graft because it is a major artery supplying the upper limb and is not suitable for harvesting.

Exam pearl:
CABG grafts:
 Internal mammary artery
 Radial artery
 Saphenous vein
❌ Brachial artery

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪) The earliest change in ECG of MI is
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The earliest ECG change in acute myocardial infarction (MI) is usually ST segment deviation (especially ST elevation in STEMI) due to acute myocardial injury and current of injury.

Sequence of ECG changes in MI:

  1. ST segment elevation/deviation → earliest change

  2. T wave inversion → later (ischemia)

  3. Pathological Q wave → indicates myocardial necrosis (hours to days)

  4. T wave changes/Q wave evolution occur subsequently

Exam pearl:
MI ECG progression:
ST elevation → T wave inversion → Pathological Q wave → T wave normalization (later).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৫) Valuable 1st aid measure in unstable angina
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The most valuable first aid measure in unstable angina is sublingual glyceryl trinitrate (GTN/nitroglycerin). It causes venodilation, reducing preload and myocardial oxygen demand, and also improves coronary blood flow, providing rapid relief of ischemic chest pain.

  • Morphine → used for severe persistent pain, but not the first measure.

  • Oxygen → only indicated if the patient is hypoxic (not routinely).

  • PCI → definitive management in selected high-risk patients, not a first aid measure.

Exam pearl:
Acute anginal chest pain → Sublingual GTN first
GTN acts by ↑ nitric oxide → ↑ cGMP → vascular smooth muscle relaxation.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৬) Pathognomonic for acute rheumatic fever
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Aschoff nodules (Aschoff bodies) are the pathognomonic histological finding of acute rheumatic fever (ARF). They are granulomatous lesions found in the myocardium, consisting of:

  • Central fibrinoid necrosis

  • Anitschkow cells ("caterpillar cells")

  • Surrounding inflammatory cells

  • Pancarditis → Common cardiac manifestation of ARF (endocardium, myocardium, pericardium), but not pathognomonic.

  • Fibrinoid degeneration → Seen in many immune-mediated diseases, not specific.

Exam pearl:
Acute rheumatic fever → Aschoff nodules = Pathognomonic lesion
Cardiac involvement → Pancarditis

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৭) Minor manifestation of rheumatic fever
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
According to Jones criteria for acute rheumatic fever, arthralgia is a minor manifestation.

Major manifestations:

  • Carditis

  • Migratory polyarthritis

  • Sydenham chorea

  • Erythema marginatum

  • Subcutaneous nodules

Minor manifestations:

  • Arthralgia

  • Fever

  • Raised ESR/CRP

  • Prolonged PR interval on ECG

Exam pearl:
Jones criteria:
Major = C P E S S → Carditis, Polyarthritis, Erythema marginatum, Subcutaneous nodules, Sydenham chorea
Minor = Fever + Arthralgia + ↑ESR/CRP + Prolonged PR interval

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৮) The dominant symptom of MS
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The dominant symptom of mitral stenosis (MS) is effort-related dyspnoea due to increased left atrial pressure, leading to pulmonary venous hypertension and pulmonary congestion. Symptoms worsen with exertion because increased heart rate shortens diastole and reduces left ventricular filling.

  • Chest pain → May occur but is not the dominant symptom.

  • Cough → Can occur due to pulmonary congestion.

  • Palpitation → Common if atrial fibrillation develops.

Exam pearl:
Mitral stenosis → Most common symptom = Exertional dyspnoea
Most common arrhythmia in MS → Atrial fibrillation.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৯) Austin Flint murmur is found in
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Austin Flint murmur is found in aortic regurgitation (AR). It is a mid-diastolic rumbling murmur heard at the apex due to the regurgitant jet from the aorta striking the anterior mitral leaflet, causing functional mitral stenosis.

  • MS → True mitral stenosis with opening snap and mid-diastolic murmur.

  • MR → Pansystolic murmur at apex.

  • TR → Pansystolic murmur at left lower sternal border.

Exam pearl:
Austin Flint murmur = Aortic regurgitation (AR)
Graham Steell murmur = Pulmonary regurgitation (often due to pulmonary hypertension).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১০) Most common cause of acute infective endocarditis
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause of acute infective endocarditis. It causes a rapidly progressive infection and commonly affects:

  • Normal heart valves

  • Prosthetic valves (especially early infection)

  • IV drug users (often tricuspid valve involvement)

Other organisms:

  • Viridans streptococci → Most common cause of subacute infective endocarditis on previously damaged valves.

  • Streptococcus gallolyticus (bovis) → Associated with colorectal carcinoma.

  • Enterococci → Often associated with urinary/GI procedures.

Exam pearl:

  • Acute infective endocarditis → Staph. aureus

  • Subacute infective endocarditis → Viridans streptococci

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১১) Pivotal investigation in infective endocarditis
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Echocardiography is the pivotal investigation in infective endocarditis (IE) because it detects vegetations on heart valves, assesses valve destruction, regurgitation, abscess formation, and cardiac complications.

  • Blood culture → Essential for identifying the causative organism and guiding antibiotic therapy, but it does not directly demonstrate valve infection.

  • ECG → May show conduction abnormalities due to abscess but is not diagnostic.

  • CXR → Limited role.

Exam pearl:
Diagnosis of infective endocarditis = Duke criteria

  • Major criterion: Positive blood culture + Evidence of endocardial involvement (Echocardiography)

  • Most important imaging test → Echocardiography.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১২) HTN with radiofemoral delay indicates
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Hypertension with radiofemoral delay is a classic sign of coarctation of the aorta. In this condition, there is narrowing of the aorta (usually near the ductus arteriosus), causing:

  • High blood pressure in upper limbs

  • Delayed and weak femoral pulses

  • Radiofemoral delay

Other options:

  • Renal artery stenosis → Causes secondary hypertension but not radiofemoral delay.

  • Polycystic kidney disease → Can cause HTN but no pulse delay.

  • Pregnancy → Not associated with radiofemoral delay.

Exam pearl:
Radiofemoral delay + HTN → Coarctation of aorta.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৩) Drug of choice in isolated systolic hypertension
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The drug of choice in isolated systolic hypertension (ISH), especially in elderly patients, is a calcium channel blocker (CCB) (particularly dihydropyridine CCBs like amlodipine).

ISH occurs due to reduced arterial compliance and increased pulse pressure. CCBs effectively reduce systolic blood pressure and have good evidence for stroke prevention in elderly hypertensive patients.

  • ACEi/ARB → Useful in many hypertensive patients, especially with diabetes or renal disease.

  • Beta blockers → Not first-line for isolated systolic hypertension unless specific indications exist.

Exam pearl:
Isolated systolic hypertension (elderly) → CCB (Amlodipine)
Common first-line antihypertensive classes: CCB, ACEi/ARB, Thiazide diuretics.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৪) Antihypertensive contraindicated in gout
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Thiazide diuretics are contraindicated (or should be avoided) in patients with gout because they decrease uric acid excretion by the kidney, causing hyperuricaemia and potentially triggering gout attacks.

  • ARB (Losartan) → Actually has a uricosuric effect and may be beneficial in gout patients.

  • CCB → Generally safe in gout.

  • Beta blockers → Not specifically contraindicated.

Exam pearl:
Gout + Hypertension → Avoid Thiazides
Preferred option → Losartan (ARB) or CCB.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৫) Drugs used in accelerated hypertension except
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
In accelerated hypertension (hypertensive emergency), drugs used for rapid blood pressure control include:

  • Labetalol (IV β-blocker with α-blocking action)

  • Hydralazine (especially in pregnancy-related hypertensive emergencies)

  • Frusemide (Furosemide) (used when there is acute pulmonary oedema/volume overload)

GTN (glyceryl trinitrate) is not a routine drug for accelerated hypertension. It is mainly used in acute coronary syndrome and acute pulmonary oedema with hypertension.

Exam pearl:
Hypertensive emergency drugs: Labetalol, Hydralazine, Sodium nitroprusside, Nicardipine, Furosemide (if fluid overload).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৬) Not a Pathognomonic feature of VT
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Extreme left axis deviation (LAD) is not a pathognomonic feature of ventricular tachycardia (VT). It may be seen in VT but is not diagnostic by itself.

Features strongly suggestive/pathognomonic of VT include:

  • Atrioventricular (AV) dissociation → atria and ventricles beating independently

  • Capture beats → occasional normal conduction from atria to ventricles

  • Fusion beats → hybrid QRS due to simultaneous ventricular and supraventricular activation

Exam pearl:
VT clues (Brugada criteria):
 AV dissociation
 Capture beats
 Fusion beats
 Extreme LAD alone is not pathognomonic.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৭) Altered colour vision is associated with toxicity of
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Digoxin toxicity is classically associated with altered colour vision (especially yellow-green vision / xanthopsia). This occurs due to effects of digoxin on the retina and visual processing pathways.

Other options:

  • GTN → Headache, hypotension, flushing.

  • Amiodarone → Corneal deposits, optic neuropathy (but not classic colour vision change).

  • Verapamil → Bradycardia, AV block, constipation.

Exam pearl:
Digoxin toxicity → Yellow vision (xanthopsia) + arrhythmias + GI symptoms.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৮) Mechanism of heart failure following MI
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Heart failure following myocardial infarction (MI) occurs mainly due to reduced ventricular contractility. MI causes death of cardiac myocytes, leading to decreased myocardial contractile function, reduced stroke volume, and impaired cardiac output.

  • Ventricular outflow obstruction → Seen in conditions like aortic stenosis, not MI-related heart failure.

  • Ventricular inflow obstruction → Seen in mitral stenosis, not typical after MI.

  • Ventricular volume overload → May occur in valvular diseases but is not the primary mechanism after MI.

Exam pearl:
MI → Myocardial necrosis → ↓ Ventricular contractility → ↓ Cardiac output → Heart failure.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৯) Features of right heart failure excludes
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Cardiomegaly is not a typical feature of right heart failure and is not considered a major clinical sign of systemic venous congestion.

Features of right-sided heart failure include:

  • Raised JVP → due to systemic venous congestion

  • Hepatomegaly → hepatic venous congestion

  • Ascites → fluid accumulation in the peritoneal cavity

  • Peripheral oedema

Cardiomegaly may occur in heart failure due to underlying cardiac disease, but it is not a specific feature of right heart failure.

Exam pearl:
Right heart failure → Raised JVP + Hepatomegaly + Ascites + Peripheral oedema.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২০) Sudden death in patient with heart failure is most probably due to
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Sudden death in patients with heart failure is most commonly due to ventricular arrhythmias, especially ventricular fibrillation (VF). A failing heart has increased electrical instability, myocardial scarring, and risk of re-entry circuits, which can precipitate fatal arrhythmias.

  • Atrial fibrillation → Common in heart failure but usually not the immediate cause of sudden cardiac death.

  • Thromboembolism → Risk is increased, especially with AF, but less common as a cause of sudden death.

  • Hypokalemia → Can trigger arrhythmias but is not the most probable cause.

Exam pearl:
Heart failure + sudden death → Ventricular tachyarrhythmia (VT/VF).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২১) ST elevation with upward concavity & PR interval depression in ECG suggests
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Acute pericarditis classically shows ECG changes of:

  • Diffuse ST segment elevation with upward concavity

  • PR interval depression (due to atrial involvement)

These findings help differentiate pericarditis from acute myocardial infarction, where ST elevation is usually localized and may have reciprocal changes.

Other options:

  • Cardiac tamponade → May show low voltage QRS and electrical alternans.

  • Acute myocarditis → Can mimic MI but PR depression is not typical.

  • Infective endocarditis → Does not produce these ECG changes.

Exam pearl:
Acute pericarditis ECG = Diffuse concave ST elevation + PR depression.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২২) Definitive investigation for pericardial effusion
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Echocardiography is the definitive investigation for pericardial effusion. It can directly visualize fluid accumulation in the pericardial space and assess:

  • Size of effusion

  • Cardiac chamber compression

  • Features of cardiac tamponade (e.g., right atrial/right ventricular collapse)

Other options:

  • ECG → May show low voltage QRS or electrical alternans but is not diagnostic.

  • CXR → May show an enlarged “water bottle” cardiac silhouette in large effusion.

  • Blood culture → Used for infection detection, not effusion diagnosis.

Exam pearl:
Pericardial effusion → Echocardiography is the investigation of choice.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৩) Clinical features of cardiac tamponade excludes
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Kussmaul’s sign is not a typical feature of cardiac tamponade. It is classically seen in constrictive pericarditis and right ventricular failure, where there is impaired right ventricular filling during inspiration.

Clinical features of cardiac tamponade (Beck’s triad):

  • Hypotension

  • Raised JVP

  • Muffled heart sounds

Other features:

  • Pulsus paradoxus (marked fall in systolic BP during inspiration)

  • Gross elevation of JVP

  • Hepatomegaly due to systemic venous congestion

Exam pearl:
Cardiac tamponade → Pulsus paradoxus + Raised JVP + Muffled heart sounds
Kussmaul sign → Constrictive pericarditis / RV failure.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৪) Most common congenital cardiac malformation
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Ventricular septal defect (VSD) is the most common congenital cardiac malformation. It is a defect in the interventricular septum causing a left-to-right shunt (initially), leading to increased pulmonary blood flow.

Other options:

  • ASD → Common congenital heart defect but less common than VSD.

  • PDA → Persistent connection between aorta and pulmonary artery; common in premature infants.

  • TOF → Most common cyanotic congenital heart disease, not the most common overall.

Exam pearl:

  • Most common congenital heart disease → VSD

  • Most common cyanotic CHD → Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৫) A continuous machinery murmur is found in
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
A continuous machinery murmur is classically heard in Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA). It occurs due to continuous blood flow from the high-pressure aorta to the pulmonary artery throughout both systole and diastole.

Other options:

  • ASD → Fixed wide split S2 with systolic flow murmur.

  • VSD → Harsh pansystolic murmur.

  • TOF → Ejection systolic murmur due to right ventricular outflow obstruction.

Exam pearl:
PDA = Continuous machinery murmur
VSD = Pansystolic murmur
ASD = Fixed wide split S2.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৬) CURB-65 scoring system is related to
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
CURB-65 is a clinical scoring system used to assess the severity of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and guide decisions regarding hospital admission and treatment intensity.

CURB-65 components:

  • C → Confusion

  • U → Urea > 7 mmol/L

  • R → Respiratory rate ≥ 30/min

  • B → Blood pressure low (SBP <90 or DBP ≤60)

  • 65 → Age ≥65 years

Other options:

  • Asthma, COPD, Bronchiectasis → Do not use CURB-65 for severity assessment.

Exam pearl:
CURB-65 = Severity assessment tool for community-acquired pneumonia.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৭) Most common infecting agent in CAP
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The most common infecting agent in community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus). It is the leading bacterial cause of CAP in adults.

Other options:

  • Staphylococcus aureus → Can cause severe pneumonia, especially after influenza.

  • Mycoplasma pneumoniae → Common cause of atypical pneumonia, especially in young adults.

  • Legionella → Causes atypical pneumonia with systemic features (e.g., hyponatraemia).

Exam pearl:
Most common cause of CAP → Streptococcus pneumoniae
Most common atypical pneumonia organism → Mycoplasma pneumoniae.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৮) Common complication of pneumonia
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The most common complication of pneumonia is para-pneumonic effusion (pleural fluid accumulation associated with pneumonia). It occurs due to inflammation spreading to the pleura and may be simple or complicated.

Other options:

  • Empyema → A complication of para-pneumonic effusion when pus accumulates in the pleural space.

  • ARDS → Severe but less common complication, especially in critically ill patients.

  • Pneumothorax → Rare complication.

Exam pearl:
Pneumonia complications:

  1. Para-pneumonic effusion (most common)

  2. Empyema

  3. Lung abscess

  4. ARDS (severe cases)

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৯) Type of hypersensitivity reaction in TB
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Tuberculosis (TB) involves a Type IV hypersensitivity reaction (Delayed-type hypersensitivity) mediated by T lymphocytes. It occurs due to a cell-mediated immune response against Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens.

  • Anaphylactic (Type I) → IgE-mediated immediate reaction (e.g., allergy, anaphylaxis)

  • Immune complex mediated (Type III) → Antigen-antibody complex deposition (e.g., serum sickness)

  • Complement based → Not a classification of hypersensitivity type

Exam pearl:
TB → Type IV hypersensitivity → Delayed T-cell mediated reaction
Mantoux test (tuberculin skin test) is also an example of Type IV hypersensitivity.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩০) Which anti-TB drug forms the cornerstone of 6-mlnths chemotherapy
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Isoniazid (INH) forms the cornerstone of 6-month anti-TB chemotherapy because it is a highly effective bactericidal drug active against rapidly dividing Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It is a key component of the standard regimen:

2 months: Isoniazid + Rifampicin + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol
4 months: Isoniazid + Rifampicin

Other options:

  • Rifampicin → Most important sterilizing drug and prevents relapse, but INH is traditionally considered the cornerstone.

  • Pyrazinamide → Effective against dormant organisms in acidic environments.

  • Ethambutol → Prevents emergence of resistance.

Exam pearl:
Cornerstone of TB treatment = Isoniazid
Most powerful sterilizing drug = Rifampicin.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩১) Most common extra-pulmonary site of TB
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The most common extra-pulmonary site of tuberculosis (TB) is the lymph node (tuberculous lymphadenitis). It is especially common in cervical lymph nodes and is often called scrofula.

Other options:

  • GIT TB → Commonly affects the ileocaecal region but less frequent.

  • Bone TB → Usually affects the spine (Pott’s disease).

  • Brain TB → Causes tuberculous meningitis, a serious but less common manifestation.

Exam pearl:
Most common extra-pulmonary TB site → Lymph node
Most common GIT TB site → Ileocaecal region.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩২) Retrobulbar neuritis is a major adverse reaction observed in therapy with
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Ethambutol causes retrobulbar neuritis, a major adverse effect due to optic nerve toxicity. It can lead to:

  • Decreased visual acuity

  • Loss of red–green colour discrimination

  • Visual field defects

Other options:

  • Isoniazid → Peripheral neuropathy (prevented by pyridoxine)

  • Pyrazinamide → Hyperuricaemia, hepatotoxicity

  • Streptomycin → Ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity

Exam pearl:
Ethambutol → Optic neuritis (red-green colour blindness)
INH → Peripheral neuropathy
Streptomycin → 8th nerve toxicity.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৩) Most common cause of bronchiactesis
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The most common cause of bronchiectasis is suppurative (severe bacterial) pneumonia, especially in the acquired forms. Recurrent or severe lower respiratory tract infections cause chronic inflammation and destruction of bronchial walls, leading to permanent bronchial dilatation.

Other options:

  • Cystic fibrosis → Important cause, especially in children and Western populations, but not the most common overall.

  • Tuberculosis → A recognized cause of bronchiectasis, especially in endemic areas.

  • Bronchial tumor → Can cause localized bronchiectasis due to obstruction but is uncommon.

Exam pearl:
Bronchiectasis → Most common cause: Suppurative pneumonia
In children → Think cystic fibrosis
In developing countries → TB is an important cause.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৪) Investigation of choice in Bronchiectasis
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest is the investigation of choice (gold standard) for bronchiectasis. It demonstrates permanent bronchial dilatation and typical features such as:

  • Signet ring sign (dilated bronchus larger than accompanying pulmonary artery)

  • Lack of bronchial tapering

  • Bronchi visible near the pleura

Other options:

  • CXR → May show tram-track shadows but has low sensitivity.

  • MRI → Not routinely used.

  • USG → Not useful for diagnosing bronchiectasis.

Exam pearl:
Bronchiectasis → HRCT chest = gold standard investigation.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৫) Amber coloured pleural fluid indicates
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Amber-coloured pleural fluid is classically associated with tuberculous pleural effusion. TB pleural fluid is usually a straw-coloured (amber) exudate with high protein and lymphocyte predominance.

Other options:

  • CCF → Usually causes transudative pleural effusion, often clear/straw coloured but not classically amber.

  • RA → May cause pleural effusion with low glucose and high LDH.

  • SLE → Can cause inflammatory pleural effusion, often serous.

Exam pearl:
TB pleural effusion → Straw/amber coloured, lymphocyte-rich exudate

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৬) Removal of more than ... L of pleural fluid at a time may risk re-expansion pulmonary injury?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Removal of more than 1.5 litres of pleural fluid at a time may increase the risk of re-expansion pulmonary oedema (re-expansion lung injury), especially when a chronically collapsed lung is rapidly re-expanded.

To reduce risk:

  • Remove fluid slowly

  • Monitor patient symptoms (chest discomfort, cough, dyspnoea)

  • Avoid excessive drainage in a single session

Other options:

  • 0.1 L, 0.5 L, 1.0 L → Usually not considered the critical volume threshold.

Exam pearl:
Thoracentesis → Avoid removing >1.5 L pleural fluid at one time due to risk of re-expansion pulmonary oedema.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৭) The combination of absent breath sound and a resonant percussion note is a diagnostic of
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The combination of absent breath sounds + resonant (hyper-resonant) percussion note is diagnostic of pneumothorax. Air accumulates in the pleural space, separating the lung from the chest wall, resulting in:

  • Reduced/absent breath sounds

  • Hyper-resonant percussion note

Other options:

  • Pleurisy → Pleural rub may be present; breath sounds usually not absent.

  • Pleural effusion → Causes stony dullness on percussion with reduced breath sounds.

  • Empyema → Causes dullness due to pus/fluid collection.

Exam pearl:

  • Pneumothorax → Absent breath sound + Hyper-resonance

  • Pleural effusion → Absent breath sound + Stony dullness

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৮) D-shaped shadow in CXR indicates
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
A D-shaped shadow on chest X-ray is classically seen in pleural effusion, particularly due to loculated pleural fluid forming a lenticular (D-shaped) opacity along the pleural surface.

Other options:

  • Pleurisy → May cause pleural thickening but not a typical D-shaped shadow.

  • Empyema → Can produce a similar lenticular opacity if loculated, but the classic association is pleural effusion.

  • Pneumothorax → Shows increased radiolucency with absent lung markings.

Exam pearl:
D-shaped/lenticular opacity on CXR → Loculated pleural effusion (especially fissural effusion).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৯) Which is the most significant risk factor for COPD
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The most significant risk factor for COPD is cigarette smoking. It is responsible for the majority of COPD cases and causes chronic airway inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, small airway narrowing, and destruction of alveolar walls (emphysema).

Other options:

  • Indoor air pollution → Important risk factor, especially in developing countries.

  • Dust exposure → Occupational exposure can contribute but is less significant.

  • Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency → A genetic cause of early-onset emphysema but uncommon.

Exam pearl:
COPD = Smoking until proven otherwise
Most important risk factor → Cigarette smoking.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪০) COPD is diagnosed when post bronchodilator spirometry shows FEV/FVC is less than
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
COPD is diagnosed when post-bronchodilator spirometry shows:

FEV₁/FVC ratio < 0.70 (70%)

This indicates persistent airflow limitation that is not fully reversible after bronchodilator use, which is the diagnostic criterion for COPD according to GOLD guidelines.

Other options:

  • 30%, 40%, 50% → Indicate more severe airflow obstruction but are not diagnostic cut-offs.

Exam pearl:
COPD diagnosis → Post-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC < 70%.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪১) Which one in central to the management of breathlessness
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Bronchodilators are central to the management of breathlessness in COPD because they reduce airway obstruction by causing bronchial smooth muscle relaxation, improving airflow and reducing dyspnoea.

Examples:

  • β₂ agonists (Salbutamol, Formoterol)

  • Antimuscarinics (Ipratropium, Tiotropium)

Other options:

  • Oxygen → Used in patients with chronic hypoxaemia, not the main treatment for breathlessness in all COPD patients.

  • Steroids → Reduce exacerbations and inflammation but are not the primary bronchodilating therapy.

  • Pulmonary rehabilitation → Improves exercise capacity and quality of life, but not the immediate central treatment.

Exam pearl:
COPD breathlessness → Bronchodilators are the cornerstone of symptomatic management.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪২) Symptoms of asthma worsens in the
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Symptoms of asthma typically worsen in the early morning hours (around 3–5 AM) due to circadian variation in airway responsiveness. During this time:

  • Airway inflammation increases

  • Cortisol levels are lowest

  • Parasympathetic (vagal) activity increases
    → causing increased bronchoconstriction and worsening symptoms.

Other options:

  • Midday/evening/early night → Symptoms may occur, but the classic worsening period is early morning.

Exam pearl:
Asthma → Early morning worsening (“morning dip”) due to circadian airway hyperreactivity.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৩) Which drug is added in initial add-on therapy step of management of asthma
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
In asthma management, when low-dose inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) alone is insufficient, the initial add-on therapy is the addition of an inhaled long-acting β₂ agonist (LABA).

  • Low-dose ICS → First-line controller therapy, not an add-on.

  • Inhaled LABA → Added to ICS to improve symptom control and reduce exacerbations.

  • LTRA (e.g., Montelukast) → Alternative add-on, especially with allergic rhinitis or aspirin-induced asthma.

  • LAMA (e.g., Tiotropium) → Usually added in more severe asthma not controlled by ICS/LABA.

Exam pearl:
Asthma step-up therapy:
Low-dose ICS → Add LABA → Increase ICS dose/add LAMA or other therapies.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৪) Feature suggesting near-fatal asthma
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
A raised PaCO₂ is a feature suggesting near-fatal asthma because it indicates respiratory muscle fatigue and impending ventilatory failure. In severe asthma, patients initially develop low PaCO₂ due to hyperventilation. A normal or rising PaCO₂ is a warning sign of deteriorating ventilation.

Other options:

  • Cyanosis → Suggests severe hypoxaemia but not the most specific indicator of near-fatal asthma.

  • Silent chest → A very severe sign indicating minimal airflow due to extreme bronchoconstriction.

  • Exhaustion → Indicates fatigue but is less specific.

Exam pearl:
Near-fatal asthma → Rising/normal PaCO₂ = impending respiratory failure
Acute severe asthma → PaCO₂ usually low; rising PaCO₂ is a danger sign.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৫) Antimicrobials causing pulmonary eosinophilia except
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Pulmonary eosinophilia is a drug-induced hypersensitivity reaction commonly associated with certain antimicrobials, especially:

  • Nitrofurantoin → Classic cause of acute/chronic pulmonary eosinophilia.

  • Tetracycline → Can cause drug-induced pulmonary eosinophilia.

  • Penicillin → May cause hypersensitivity reactions including eosinophilic lung disease.

Erythromycin is not a typical cause of pulmonary eosinophilia.

Exam pearl:
Drug-induced eosinophilic pneumonia causes:
 Nitrofurantoin (most classic)
 Tetracyclines
 Penicillins
❌ Erythromycin (not typical)

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৬) Causes of chronic type-2 respiratory failure excludes
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Chronic type 2 respiratory failure is characterized by persistent hypercapnia (↑ PaCO₂), usually due to alveolar hypoventilation.

Causes include:

  • COPD → Common cause due to airflow obstruction and ventilatory failure.

  • Sleep apnoea → Causes chronic hypoventilation and CO₂ retention.

  • Myopathies → Respiratory muscle weakness leads to hypoventilation.

Lobar collapse (atelectasis) is usually an acute/reversible condition causing hypoxaemia (Type 1 respiratory failure), not a typical cause of chronic type 2 respiratory failure.

Exam pearl:
Type 2 respiratory failure = “pump failure” → COPD + neuromuscular disease + obesity hypoventilation + sleep apnoea.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৭) Most common cell type of lung cancer
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The most common cell type of lung cancer overall is adenocarcinoma. It is now the most common subtype of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and is frequently seen in:

  • Peripheral regions of the lung

  • Non-smokers and females (although smokers can also develop it)

Other options:

  • Squamous cell carcinoma → Previously most common; strongly associated with smoking and usually central bronchus.

  • Small-cell carcinoma → Highly aggressive, associated with smoking, causes paraneoplastic syndromes.

  • Large-cell carcinoma → Less common subtype of NSCLC.

Exam pearl:

  • Most common lung cancer overall → Adenocarcinoma

  • Most common lung cancer in smokers (classic teaching) → Squamous cell carcinoma

  • Most aggressive lung cancer → Small-cell carcinoma.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৮) Non metastatic extra pulmonary effect that is usually associated with small-cell lung cancer
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is classically associated with paraneoplastic syndrome due to ectopic hormone production. The most common non-metastatic extrapulmonary effect is:

  • SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone secretion) → due to ectopic ADH production, causing:

    • Hyponatraemia

    • Low serum osmolality

    • Concentrated urine

Other options:

  • Carcinoid syndrome → More commonly associated with carcinoid tumours (neuroendocrine tumors), not typical SCLC.

  • Gynaecomastia → Not a classic SCLC association.

  • Hypercalcaemia → Classically associated with squamous cell carcinoma due to PTHrP secretion.

Exam pearl:

  • Small-cell lung cancer → SIADH + Ectopic ACTH production

  • Squamous cell lung cancer → Hypercalcaemia (PTHrP).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৯) The most frequent symptom of respiratory disease
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Cough is the most frequent symptom of respiratory disease. It is a protective reflex that helps clear secretions, foreign particles, and irritants from the respiratory tract. It is commonly seen in conditions such as:

  • Upper respiratory tract infections

  • Asthma

  • COPD

  • Pneumonia

  • Bronchiectasis

Other options:

  • Chest pain → Occurs in pleurisy, pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, etc., but is less common.

  • Breathlessness → A common symptom but not the most frequent overall.

  • Haemoptysis → Important symptom but less common.

Exam pearl:
Most common respiratory symptom → Cough
Most common symptom of COPD → Breathlessness (dyspnoea).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৫০) Which disease occurs less frequently in smokers
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Sarcoidosis occurs less frequently in smokers. Smoking is not a risk factor for sarcoidosis and has been observed to have an inverse association with the disease.

Other options:

  • COPD → Strongly associated with cigarette smoking (major risk factor).

  • Lung cancers → Strongly associated with smoking.

  • Myocardial infarction (MI) → Smoking is a major modifiable cardiovascular risk factor.

Exam pearl:
Smoking increases risk of: COPD, lung cancer, MI.
Smoking is inversely associated with: Sarcoidosis.
